title: Proactive Headroom Negotiator and Fallback Orchestration PRD
creator: Ava Chen
overview: Enable a proactive headroom negotiation and fallback orchestration layer for Dedicated capacity customers. This feature coordinates temporary headroom acquisition, graceful SLA-aware fallback to compatible model variants or regions, and provides audit trails and telemetry for billing and incident analysis.
background: Dedicated customers require predictable latency and throughput. Sudden surges or noisy neighbors risk violated SLAs or expensive overprovisioning. Existing features address reactive burst and emergency preemption but lack a controlled negotiation flow that (1) lets tenants request short-lived headroom with explicit cost/latency tradeoffs, (2) auto-negotiates fallback policies when headroom cannot be granted, and (3) surfaces decisions in telemetry and billing records.
problem_statement: We need a controllable, observable orchestration that reduces SLA violations during transient surges while limiting cost exposure and avoiding noisy-neighbor side effects. Current autoscale and reserve mechanisms either block requests, silently degrade latency, or overcommit capacity without clear tenant-visible decisioning.
goals: Provide an API & control-plane flow for tenants to request transient headroom with constraints (max cost, max latency degradation, fallback policy)
Implement an orchestration engine that attempts staged mitigations: local autoscale, borrow from soft reserves, route to compatible model variant, route to alternate region, or queue with backoff
Ensure every decision is auditable and emits standardized telemetry for billing, SLO reporting, and post-incident analysis
Offer tenant-facing UI controls in Console for default fallback policies and per-route overrides
non_goals: Replacing long-term capacity reservations or changing committed-contract billing models
Providing unlimited cross-tenant bursting that violates isolation guarantees
Implementing new kernel/runtime optimizations (handled by runtime team separately)
user_stories: As a tenant admin, I can set a default headroom policy that caps additional spend per-minute and preferred fallback behaviors
As an SRE, I can inspect the headroom negotiation history for a tenant and see decision timestamps, costs, and chosen fallback path
As a product engineer, my route can opt into optimistic headroom negotiation to reduce 429s with clear cost attribution
As an on-call responder, I receive an alert when fallback to a lower-tier model or region exceeds a configured rate
functional_requirements: FR-1: New HEADROOM_REQUEST API that accepts: tenant_id, route, requested_capacity (qps or tokens/sec), max_cost_per_minute, max_latency_increase_ms, fallback_order (ordered list of strategies), request_id
FR-2: Orchestration engine performs staged checks and actions in order: local autoscale (if available), soft-reserve borrow, model-variant failover, region failover, queuing with jittered backoff
FR-3: If any stage succeeds, return decision with reason, estimated cost delta, and TTL for headroom allocation
FR-4: If orchestration fails or times out, apply tenant's fallback policy and return a structured failure response for SDKs and Console
FR-5: Emit an immutable negotiation log entry for every HEADROOM_REQUEST and decision, retained for 90 days (configurable by enterprise add-on)
FR-6: Console UI: policy editor for default tenant fallback rules and per-route overrides, and a negotiator activity feed
FR-7: Billing export: include headroom charge items with request_id and decision_reason for downstream invoicing
non_functional_requirements: NFR-1: Decision latency for orchestration pipeline must be <= 200ms added to request path for synchronous requests; asynchronous prefetch flows allowed up to 2s
NFR-2: Telemetry event emission must be reliable (>=99.9% delivery to internal event bus) and idempotent
NFR-3: Orchestration component must scale horizontally and tolerate transient loss of downstream services (graceful degrade to conservative fallback)
NFR-4: Audit logs must be tamper-evident and include cryptographic hash chain id for each negotiation (first iteration can be simple append-only with checksums)
metrics: SLO: Reduce tenant-facing 429/503 incidents due to sudden surges by 35% for customers using headroom negotiator within 90 days
Cost: Average added headroom spend per incident should be <= configured max_cost_per_minute for 95% of decisions
Latency: Mean increase in p50 latency for affected routes should be <= configured max_latency_increase_ms
Reliability: Orchestration decision path successful (granted headroom or applied fallback) in 99.5% of HEADROOM_REQUESTs
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: HEADROOM_REQUEST API implemented with schema validation and returns deterministic decision payloads
AC-2: Orchestration engine executes the staged mitigation order and chooses the first successful option; unit/integration tests cover each stage and failure modes
AC-3: Negotiation logs are written to the centralized event bus and can be queried by request_id from Console within 30s
AC-4: Console exposes policy editor and an activity feed; UI tests verify policy persistence and overwrite behavior
AC-5: Billing export contains headroom line-items with request_id, tenant_id, decision_reason, and cost_delta for all granted headroom events
AC-6: End-to-end load test simulating tenant surge demonstrates at least 25% fewer SLA violations compared to baseline (no negotiator), and telemetry matches metrics target
AC-7: Security review completed and data in negotiation logs redacted for PII before export
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha (QA + 3 enterprise customers) behind feature flag for selected accounts. Phase 2: Incremental opt-in in Console for all Dedicated customers with telemetry enabled. Phase 3: On-by-default for customers with committed capacity and explicit opt-out. Phased rollout to small cohorts first, monitor cost, latency and alert volumes, and gradually expand over 6-8 weeks.
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit events: headroom.requested, headroom.decision, headroom.granted, headroom.rejected, headroom.fallback_applied
Create dashboards: per-tenant headroom spend, negotiated headroom TTLs, fallback frequency by strategy
Alerts: high fallback rate (>5% of requests) for a tenant over 10 minutes, headroom spend burn exceeding tenant-defined budget, orchestration error-rate >1%
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Tenants may accidentally set permissive max_cost_per_minute and incur large bills. Mitigation: require billing cap confirmation in Console and default conservative limits
Risk: Overly aggressive region failover increases p99 latency. Mitigation: prioritize model-variant failover before region failover and expose per-route latency budgets
Risk: Orchestration becomes a single point of failure. Mitigation: design for graceful degradation to conservative fallback (deny or queue) and replicate orchestration across zones
open_questions: Q1: Should HEADROOM_REQUEST be synchronous on the request path or primarily an asynchronous prefetch API? Hybrid recommended — support both flows
Q2: How do we attribute billing when headroom is granted across tenants in soft-reserve borrow scenarios? Proposal: mark costs against borrower with audit link to lender for internal chargebacks
Q3: What TTL granularity is optimal (seconds vs minutes)? Start with 30s/60s/5m presets and iterate based on telemetry
implementation_notes: Collaborate with Runtime team to expose hooks for local autoscale and with Billing to define export schema. Engineering to provide a mock orchestration in dev env for Console integration tests. Provide a migration doc for existing burst policies explaining interactions.
